rubrics.criterion: The request-assembly inputs (HTTP method, request URL, decoded body, raw event method, and raw event path) are carried by a single shared abstraction used by all three request flavors, instead of being passed as the same five separate parameters through each request accessor's assembly signature.
rubrics.rationale: The request-assembly group is the largest recurring parameter group in this task and spans all three request flavors; collapsing it is the central outcome the task asks for, regardless of the specific record type or constructor name chosen.

rubrics.criterion: The response-assembly inputs (status, headers, encoded body, and base64 flag) are carried by a single shared abstraction used by all three response writers, instead of being passed as the same four separate parameters through each writer's response-assembly signature.
rubrics.rationale: The response-assembly group is the symmetric counterpart on the response side and recurs across all three response writers; consolidating it is required to resolve the relation on the response path.

rubrics.criterion: The query-string parameter group and the request-header-propagation parameter group that are shared by the REST API v1 and ALB flavors are each consolidated so the same parameters no longer repeat across the two flavors' matching signatures.
rubrics.rationale: These two recurring three-parameter groups appear on the REST API and ALB request accessors; resolving them is part of removing the parameter-list duplication beyond the two largest groups.

rubrics.criterion: Every call site that previously threaded the consolidated parameter groups as separate parameters is updated to construct and pass the new abstraction, with no remaining call that passes the old individual parameters to a consolidated stage.
rubrics.rationale: A sound repair must update all call sites consistently; leftover calls that still pass the individual parameters indicate the abstraction was added but not actually adopted.

rubrics.criterion: No request or response flavor is left with its own duplicate of a parameter group that the solver consolidated for the other flavors (for example, only one or two of the three request accessors moved off the request-assembly parameter list while the third still carries it).
rubrics.rationale: Partially covering the flavors leaves the same data still traveling as separate parameters through the remaining signatures and re-introduces the duplication the task targets; this failure mode is specific to a multi-flavor pipeline where each owner can be missed.

rubrics.criterion: Flavor-specific stages that genuinely differ across flavors — the v2 raw query-string handling, the v2 single-value header propagation, and the ALB host resolution that does not honor the custom-host override — remain expressed per flavor rather than being forced into a shared abstraction that erases the documented difference.
rubrics.rationale: The task asks to consolidate shared stages, not to merge genuinely divergent ones; preserving flavor-specific behavior is a sign the abstraction boundary was chosen well.

rubrics.criterion: No signature in the core package still declares the former multi-parameter request-assembly, response-assembly, query-string, or header-propagation groups as separate parameters; the per-flavor helpers that existed only to carry those parameter lists have been removed or replaced by the shared abstractions.
rubrics.rationale: Leaving the old multi-parameter signatures in place keeps the recurring parameter groups present even after introducing an abstraction, so the leftover signatures must be cleaned up.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave a newly introduced record, struct, or helper that is declared but never constructed or called by any conversion path.
rubrics.rationale: An abstraction that nothing uses is dead code added during the repair; its presence is a concrete cleanup failure rather than a generic style concern.

rubrics.criterion: The repository builds and the full test suite passes after the change, using the recorded build and test commands.
rubrics.rationale: Behavior preservation is the hard constraint on this refactor; the test suite is the deterministic witness that the conversion behavior was not altered.

rubrics.criterion: The custom-host override behavior is preserved exactly: the GO_API_HOST override is honored for both API Gateway flavors and is not honored for the ALB flavor, as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: Host resolution differs by flavor by design; a refactor that silently unifies host handling would change observable request URLs for one or more flavors.

rubrics.criterion: The change does not alter the public API of the core package or break compilation of any adapter package that delegates to core.
rubrics.rationale: The core package is consumed by many thin adapter wrappers; widening, renaming, or removing public symbols would break those callers and is out of scope for this consolidation.
